posts.title: China's biggest auto recall hits Tesla, Xiaomi, Leapmotor and others over door escape risk
posts.summary:
Multiple automakers, including Tesla, Xiaomi, Geely, Leapmotor and Xpeng, filed recall plans on the same day, covering more than 7 million vehicles in total.
For details, please visit CnEVPost (cnev.co).
bullets: Chinese regulators have initiated the largest recall in industry history, covering over 7 million vehicles across multiple brands including Tesla, Xiaomi, and Xpeng.
The primary issue involves interior emergency mechanical door releases that are difficult to identify, posing a safety risk during post-crash rescue operations.
Tesla accounts for the majority of the recall volume, with over 5.7 million vehicles affected by door release and driver attention monitoring software updates.

posts.title: CPCA sees China August NEV retail sales at about 1.04 million, penetration may hit record
posts.summary:
China's passenger NEV retail sales are expected to rise about 9.4% from July, with retail penetration reaching 65.8%.
For details, please visit CnEVPost (cnev.co).
bullets: China's passenger NEV retail sales are projected to reach 1.04 million units in August, marking a 9.4% sequential increase despite a broader automotive market decline of 21.7% year-on-year.
NEV retail penetration is expected to hit a record 65.8%, underscoring the segment's role as the primary driver of demand in an otherwise weak consumer environment.
Market activity showed a mid-month recovery driven by new model launches at the Chengdu Auto Show and the easing of weather-related disruptions, though overall consumer fundamentals remain subdued.

posts.title: BYD debuts third-gen Tang SUV, launch set for Q4
posts.summary:
The five-seat SUV will form a dual-flagship SUV lineup with the full-size Da Tang, as BYD seeks to revitalize the Tang series amid falling sales.
For details, please visit CnEVPost (cnev.co).
bullets: BYD debuted the third-generation Tang SUV, which will form a dual-flagship lineup with the existing Da Tang to revitalize the series' declining sales.
The new model features advanced 800-volt flash charging technology, capable of reaching 70% charge in just 5 minutes under normal conditions.
Equipped with the 'God's Eye B' driver-assistance system and LiDAR, the third-gen Tang is positioned as a high-tech flagship for the Dynasty series.

posts.title: Chip Industry Week In Review
posts.summary:
New Micron lab; chip/AI price jump; multi-die monitoring; cryo links for quantum chips; interconnect RC bottleneck; 18A win; CPO roadmap; 2 new CEOs; humanoid readiness gap; Hot Interconnects.
The post Chip Industry Week In Review appeared first on Semiconductor Engineering.
bullets: Foundry pricing is trending upward, with Samsung increasing costs for 4nm, 5nm, and 8nm nodes by up to 15% while SMIC also implements price hikes.
Intel Foundry secured a significant win as Socionext added the 18A-P process to its custom-SoC roadmap for high-performance AI and data center chiplets.
Marvell is deepening its partnership with Google to develop custom silicon for the TPU ecosystem, supported by a potential $12.2 billion stock purchase agreement.
Nvidia is aggressively expanding data center infrastructure through a $1.5 billion investment in SB Energy and a strategic partnership with Cloverleaf Infrastructure to secure power for U.S. sites.
Capital investment in AI hardware remains robust, highlighted by Etched raising $700 million for inference systems and YMTC’s parent company seeking $4.9 billion via a Shanghai IPO for NAND R&D.

posts.title: When AI designs a drug, who gets the credit?
posts.summary: When the biotech company Insilico Medicine used its computer models to propose a promising drug for pulmonary fibrosis, it enthusiastically claimed in a press release that the molecule had been “discovered by” its generative AI platform. Insilico leads a pack of companies using AI to rapidly come up with drug ideas humans might never think…
bullets: Biotech firms like Insilico Medicine are utilizing generative AI to accelerate drug discovery, yet they must name human inventors to secure patent protection.
US courts have consistently ruled that AI cannot be listed as an inventor on patents, as current statutes define an 'individual' strictly as a human being.
Legal experts anticipate that patent law will require significant evolution as AI systems move toward greater autonomy in the invention process.
